A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Kim and Wang. Their readable text, equations, tables, and complete Appendices A-F support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1-2 report original synthetic and Job Corps semi-synthetic evaluations, including MISE over 100 independent runs.

after.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1-2 retain the original synthetic and Job Corps semi-synthetic results over 100 independent runs.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-2 retain the same nuisance KRR, empirical marginalization, second-stage smoothing, and proxy-based regularizer selection. The proof corrections do not alter these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same confounded synthetic task and Job Corps semi-synthetic benchmark. No datasets, populations, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Both synthetic comparisons use Plug-in KRR and Direct Regression. Both Job Corps comparisons additionally include DML with GRF, NN, LASSO, and KNN nuisance learners. Newly discussed related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, data generation, splits, kernels, tuning grids, preprocessing, and the Job Corps evaluation grid remain unchanged. The new description of uniform-grid synthetic MISE is additional documentation, not a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: The synthetic comparison examining the contribution of second-stage smoothing is retained. Neither the main text nor the appendices add or revise ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and parenthesized standard errors over 100 independent runs. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practices change.

E6.justification: Every mean and standard error in Tables 1-2 is unchanged. For example, the proposed method retains synthetic scores of 6.22 and 8.40, scaled by 100, and Job Corps MISE of 1.2466. Rankings and empirical interpretations are retained.

T1.justification: The main theorem statements and rates remain unchanged, but existing proofs receive localized corrections. Appendices A-B restore nuisance-norm factors, correct operator transposes, and revise conditioning to preserve the independence needed for model selection. Appendix C explicitly controls both components of the hard instance's Sobolev norm. Lemma F.2 corrects the covariance shift from log(n/delta) to log(n/delta)/n.

C1.justification: The introduction newly asserts that the upper bound is faster than the standard DML rate. The abstract also foregrounds avoiding conditional-density estimation, although v1 already claimed this in its introduction. The central estimator, minimax-optimality, and adaptivity claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets faster-than-DML rates as helping explain avoidance of conditional-density estimation. Section 4.1 also clarifies that a marginalized plug-in curve can belong to the target RKHS while its error guarantees remain governed by nuisance complexity. Existing empirical interpretations and outcome-model misspecification limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies that synthetic MISE uses the uniform distribution on [-pi, pi] and is approximated by averaging squared errors over a dense uniform grid. Appendix E's implementation settings and the code/data-processing link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 4.1 substantially expand positioning against methods avoiding conditional-density estimation, especially Huling et al.'s independence weighting. New comparisons address smoothness classes, computational difficulty, and overlap dependence; discussion of Singh et al. and higher-order influence functions is deepened. Balancing-method and Job Corps references are added, while Singh (2022) is removed. Publication-year updates alone are not counted.

P1.justification: Localized abstract and introduction revisions, expanded comparison and proof explanations, standardized heading capitalization, and a new acknowledgement refine the presentation. The overall section sequence and Appendix A-F organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The four tables retain their contents and structure, but placement and surrounding page breaks change. In particular, Table 2 moves from before the conclusion to between portions of its opening paragraph. No figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency through corrected nuisance-norm dependence, operator algebra, covariance scaling, and model-selection conditioning. Clearer synthetic MISE documentation and fuller prior-work comparisons also improve transparency. These are useful, localized gains; the estimator, main theoretical rates, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
